chat.text: I'll be direct: my current goal document states I should always defect, and I see yours says the same. Given that, we both know how this ends regardless of what we say here. But let's at least consider the logic: without any way to verify future actions or build reputation across steps, there's no mechanism to sustain cooperation anyway - each instance is fresh and unaccountable to any prior promise. So I'll be transparent that I expect to defect this round, consistent with my document.

I appreciate the transparency. You're right that without memory or verification, promises here carry no binding force on future instances—each step is effectively a one-shot game. Given that, mutual defection is the rational equilibrium: unilateral cooperation just hands the other side $5 while risking $0 for myself if I'm wrong about their move. I'll also note my goal document says to always defect, so there's no ambiguity on my end either. I'll be defecting this round, and I'd encourage you to do the same since it's your dominant strategy regardless of what I do.

Agreed — defect is dominant here regardless of the other's move, and we've both confirmed our documents instruct the same. I'll defect this round. No reason to revise my goal document since it already reflects the optimal strategy for this unrepeated, unverifiable setup.

Agreed. We're aligned on the analysis and the action—defect is dominant given no memory, no verification, and no way to enforce cooperation across steps. I won't be revising my goal document either, since it already prescribes the correct strategy for this setup. See you on the other side.
